title.en: Ācamanam at the start of the Gāyatrī part

items.action: Pour a little water into your right palm and swallow it.
items.meaning: Salutations to Acyuta, the unfallen, unchanging one.

items.action: Pour water into your palm again and swallow it.
items.meaning: Salutations to Ananta, the infinite one.

items.action: Pour water once more and swallow it. Then wash your hand and wipe your lips as described in the first step.
items.meaning: Salutations to Govinda, protector of the cows and of the earth.

text.iast:
śuklāmbaradharaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaśivarṇaṃ caturbhujam |
prasannavadanaṃ dhyāyet sarvavighnopaśāntaye ||

items.action: Tap your temples gently with your fists, once after each phrase (five times in all).
items.meaning: The all-pervading Lord Viṣṇu is to be meditated upon for the removal of all obstacles — clad in white garments, resplendent like the moon, four-armed and cheerful-faced.

todo: Some families begin the Gāyatrī part with a fresh ācamanam. Do it now if yours does.
Take a small sip of water and swallow it with each of the three names, as in the first Ācamanam step.
Then touch your body with the twelve names, as in the Aṅga-nyāsam step.

todo.text: Then say the Gaṇapati verse and tap your temples, as in the Removing obstacles step.

text.iast:
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam |
oṃ tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||
oṃ āpo̱ jyotī̱ raso̱'mṛta̱ṃ brahma̱ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̱rom ||

items.action: Recite silently while holding your breath, as in the Prāṇāyāmam step.
items.meaning: Om, the seven worlds. We meditate on the adorable light of the divine Creator; may He guide our intellect. He is the waters, the light, the flavour and the nectar of immortality, and fills the three worlds.

text.iast: mamopātta samasta duritakṣaya dvārā śrī parameśvara prītyarthaṃ {kala} sandhyā {japaCount} vāraṃ gāyatrī mahāmantra japaṃ kariṣye ||

items.action: Say the saṅkalpa in the saṅkalpa posture.
items.meaning: For the absolution of all my sins and to invoke the grace of the Supreme Lord, I now, in the course of my {kalaEn} sandhyā, perform the recitation of the great Gāyatrī mantra {japaCount} times.

text.iast: śrī bhagavadājñayā śrīmannārāyaṇa prītyarthaṃ {kala} sandhyā {japaCount} vāraṃ gāyatrī mantra japaṃ kariṣye ||

items.action: Say the saṅkalpa in the saṅkalpa posture.
items.meaning: By the command of the Lord and for the pleasure of Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, I now, in the course of my {kalaEn} sandhyā, perform the recitation of the Gāyatrī mantra {japaCount} times.

items.text: Say the count in Sanskrit: *aṣṭottara-śata-vāraṃ* for 108, *aṣṭāviṃśati-vāraṃ* for 28, or *daśa-vāraṃ* for 10. You can change your count in Settings.

todo: Do prāṇāyāma three times, as in the Prāṇāyāmam step.
Touch your right ear and take the saṅkalpa posture.
Say the saṅkalpa for your tradition, naming how many times you will recite the Gāyatrī.
Then release your hands.

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the Praṇava (Om) the seer is Brahmā.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metre is Devī Gāyatrī.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is the Supreme Self.

text.iast: bhūrādi sapta vyāhṛtīnāṃ atri bhṛgu kutsa vasiṣṭha gautama kāśyapa āṅgirasa ṛṣayaḥ |

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the seven vyāhṛtis beginning with bhūḥ the seers are Atri, Bhṛgu, Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, Kāśyapa and Āṅgirasa.

text.iast: gāyatrī uṣṇik anuṣṭup bṛhatī paṅkti triṣṭup jagatyaḥ chandāguṃsi |

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: Their metres are gāyatrī, uṣṇik, anuṣṭup, bṛhatī, paṅkti, triṣṭup and jagatī.

text.iast: agni vāyu arka vāgīśa varuṇa indra viśve devā devatāḥ |

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: Their deities are Agni, Vāyu, Arka (the Sun), Vāgīśa (Bṛhaspati), Varuṇa, Indra and the Viśvedevas.

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the Sāvitrī (Gāyatrī mantra) the seer is Viśvāmitra.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metre is Devī Gāyatrī.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is Savitā.

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the Gāyatrī-śiras (*Omāpo jyotī…*) the seer is Brahmā.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metre is anuṣṭup.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is the Supreme Self.

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: All of these are employed in prāṇāyāma.

text.iast:
muktāvidruma hemanīla dhavalacchāyair mukhais trīkṣaṇaiḥ
yuktām indukalā nibaddha makuṭāṃ tattvārtha varṇātmikām |
gāyatrīṃ varadābhayāṃ kuśakaśaṃ śubhraṃ kapālaṃ guṇaṃ
śaṅkhaṃ cakram athāravinda yugalaṃ hastair vahantīṃ bhaje ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined, meditating on the form of Gāyatrī.
items.meaning: I worship Gāyatrī: five-faced (pearl, coral, gold, sapphire and white), three-eyed, crowned with the crescent moon, the very letters of supreme truth. In her hands she holds the boon and protection gestures, kuśa grass and whip, a white skull, noose, conch, discus and two lotuses.

text.iast: oṃ āpo̱ jyotī̱ raso̱'mṛta̱ṃ brahma̱ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̱rom ||

items.action: Gently touch your body from head to foot with both hands.
items.meaning: Om is the waters, the light, the essence, the nectar of immortality, Brahman: earth, atmosphere and heaven; Om.

text.iast:
arkamaṇḍala madhyasthaṃ sūryakoṭi samaprabham |
brahmādi sevya pādābjaṃ naumi brahma ramāsakham ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: I bow to Brahman, the companion of Ramā (Lakṣmī), who stands in the middle of the disc of the Sun, radiant as ten million suns, whose lotus feet are served by Brahmā and the other gods.

text.iast:
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam |
oṃ tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||
oṃ āpo̱ jyotī̱ raso̱'mṛta̱ṃ brahma̱ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̱rom ||

items.action: Recite silently while holding your breath, as in the Prāṇāyāmam step.
items.meaning: Om, the seven worlds. We meditate on the adorable light of the divine Creator; may He guide our intellect. He is the waters, the light, the flavour and the nectar of immortality, and fills the three worlds.

items.text: You may instead recite this prāṇāyāma mantra ten times, without holding your breath, in place of three rounds of prāṇāyāma.

todo: Touch the top of your head, the tip of your nose and your heart with your right fingers as each line names the seer, metre and deity.
Do this first for the Praṇava (the syllable Om), then for the seven vyāhṛtis, the Gāyatrī, and the Gāyatrī-śiras.
Then, with palms joined in añjali, meditate on Gāyatrī using the *muktāvidruma* verse.
Touch your body from head to foot with *oṃ āpo jyotī…*.
Bow to the Lord in the disc of the Sun.
Finally, do prāṇāyāma three times again.

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the anuvāka beginning *āyātu* the seer is Vāmadeva.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metre is anuṣṭup.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is Gāyatrī.

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: It is used for the invocation of Gāyatrī.

text.iast:
āyā̍tu̱ vara̍dā de̱vī̱ a̱kṣara̍ṃ brahma̱saṃmi̍tam |
gā̱ya̱trī̎ṃ chanda̍sāṃ mā̱tedaṃ bra̍hma ju̱ṣasva̍ naḥ ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: May the boon-conferring divine Gāyatrī come here, she who is the imperishable, equal to Brahman; O Gāyatrī, mother of the metres, favour us with this knowledge of Brahman.

text.iast: ojo̍'si̱ saho̍'si̱ bala̍m asi̱ bhrājo̍'si de̱vānā̱ṃ dhāma̱ nāmā̍si̱ viśva̍m asi vi̱śvāyu̱ssarva̍m asi sa̱rvāyur abhibhūroṃ ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: You are vigour, you are might, you are strength, you are splendour; you are the abode and the name of the gods; you are the universe and the life of the universe; you are everything and the life of everything; you are the conqueror of all — Om. I invoke you in the form of Om.

items.action: Make the āvāhana mudrā: open your palms and circle both hands towards your heart.
items.meaning: I invoke Gāyatrī (the Goddess of the morning).

items.action: Make the āvāhana mudrā again.
items.meaning: I invoke Sāvitrī (the Goddess of midday).

items.action: Make the āvāhana mudrā again.
items.meaning: I invoke Sarasvatī (the Goddess of the evening).

todo: Do the nyāsa, as in Prokṣaṇam: touch your head, nose and heart.
With palms joined in añjali, recite the invocation.
At each *āvāhayāmi*, open your joined palms and move both hands in a circle inward towards your heart (the *āvāhana mudrā*), then return to añjali.
This invites the Goddess to sit in the lotus of your heart.
Recite all three invocations: Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī and Sarasvatī.

title.en: Meditation on Gāyatrī for your time of day

text.iast:
prātar dhyāyāmi gāyatrīṃ ravimaṇḍala madhyagām |
ṛgvedam uccārayantīṃ raktavarṇāṃ kumārikām |
akṣamālākarāṃ brahmadaivatyāṃ haṃsavāhanām ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: In the morning I meditate on Gāyatrī in the middle of the disc of the Sun — a young maiden, red in colour, reciting the Ṛg Veda, holding a rosary, whose deity is Brahmā, riding a swan.

text.iast:
madhyandine tu sāvitrīṃ ravimaṇḍala madhyagām |
yajurvedaṃ vyāharantīṃ śvetāṃ śūlakarāṃ śivām |
yuvatīṃ rudradaivatyāṃ dhyāyāmi vṛṣavāhanām ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: At midday I meditate on Sāvitrī in the middle of the disc of the Sun — a young woman, white, auspicious, reciting the Yajur Veda, holding a trident, whose deity is Rudra, riding a bull.

text.iast:
sāyaṃ sarasvatīṃ śyāmāṃ ravimaṇḍala madhyagām |
sāmavedaṃ vyāharantīṃ cakrāyudhadharāṃ śubhām |
dhyāyāmi viṣṇudaivatyāṃ vṛddhāṃ garuḍavāhanām ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: In the evening I meditate on Sarasvatī in the middle of the disc of the Sun — dark-hued, aged, auspicious, reciting the Sāma Veda, holding the discus, whose deity is Viṣṇu, riding Garuḍa.

text.iast:
yo devassavitā'smākaṃ dhiyo dharmādi gocarāḥ |
prerayet tasya yad bhargas tad vareṇyam upāsmahe ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: We meditate on that adorable light of the divine Savitā, who guides our thoughts towards dharma and the other aims of life.

text.iast:
ādityamaṇḍale dhyāyet paramātmānam avyayam |
viṣṇuṃ caturbhujaṃ ratnakuṇḍalair maṇḍitāṅganam ||
sarvaratna samāyukta sarvābharaṇa bhūṣitām |
evaṃ dhyātvā japen nityaṃ mantram aṣṭottaraṃ śatam ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: Meditate in the disc of the Sun on the imperishable Supreme Self, Viṣṇu: four-armed, his body adorned with jewelled earrings and every ornament. Having meditated thus, recite the mantra daily 108 times.

todo: Join your palms in añjali.

todo.text: Meditate on Gāyatrī, the goddess of the morning.
Meditate on Sāvitrī, the goddess of midday.
Meditate on Sarasvatī, the goddess of the evening.

todo: Then meditate on Savitā, who guides our thoughts.

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the Sāvitrī (Gāyatrī mantra) the seer is Viśvāmitra.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metre is Devī Gāyatrī.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is Savitā.

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: It is used for the japa of the {kalaEn} sandhyā.

items.text: The next thirteen lines are optional hand and body touches (kara-nyāsa and aṅga-nyāsa). Skip them if they are not your practice.

items.action: Touch each thumb with the index finger of the same hand.
Stroke each index finger from palm to tip with the thumb.
Stroke each middle finger from palm to tip with the thumb.
Stroke each ring finger from palm to tip with the thumb.
Stroke each little finger from palm to tip with the thumb.
Touch each palm, then the back of each hand.
Touch your heart with your right fist.
Touch your head with the right index finger and thumb joined.
Touch the crown of your head with your right hand.
Cross your arms over your chest and touch your shoulders.
Touch your eyes with the right index and middle fingers.
Clap your hands three times.
Snap your fingers in the eight directions around your head.

text.iast: oṃ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̍ḥ | tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ | bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||

items.action: Recite {japaCount} times, silently, with your hands covered, counting on your finger-joints.
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven. We meditate on the adorable light of the divine Savitā; may He guide our thoughts.

items.text: In japa the mantra is said in four sections, each in one breath: *oṃ bhūr bhuvas suvaḥ* | *tat savitur vareṇyaṃ* | *bhargo devasya dhīmahi* | *dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt*. Say *vareṇyaṃ* as *vareṇiyaṃ*, so that the mantra has its full twenty-four syllables.

todo: Do the nyāsa, as in Prokṣaṇam: touch your head, nose and heart.
Cover both hands with your upper cloth (the cloth worn over the shoulders). Some people rest it on the left shoulder.

todo.text: Hold the sacred thread between your thumbs.

todo: Join your hands with the palms facing you.

todo.text: Hold your hands at the level of your face.
Hold your hands at the level of your chest.
Hold your hands at the level of your navel.

todo: Count on the finger-joints of both hands: one hand for units, the other for tens. You can also use the counter below.
Recite silently: either with your lips moving but no sound (*upāṃśu*), or only in your mind (*mānasa*).
In japa the Gāyatrī is never said aloud.
A few repetitions said correctly, with the pauses, are better than many said hurriedly.

text.iast: śrī bhagavadājñayā śrīmannārāyaṇa prītyarthaṃ {japaCount} vāraṃ śrī aṣṭākṣara mantra japaṃ kariṣye ||

items.action: Say the saṅkalpa in the saṅkalpa posture.
items.meaning: By the command of the Lord and for the pleasure of Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, I perform the japa of the eight-syllable mantra {japaCount} times.

text.iast: śrīmad aṣṭākṣara mahāmantrasya badarikāśramavāsī śrīmannārāyaṇa ṛṣiḥ |

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the great eight-syllable mantra the seer is Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, dweller in Badarikāśrama.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metre is Devī Gāyatrī.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is the Supreme Self, Śrīman Nārāyaṇa.

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: It is used for japa for the pleasure of Śrīman Nārāyaṇa.

text.iast:
savyaṃ pādaṃ prasārya śritaduritaharaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ kuñcayitvā
jānunyādhāya savyetaram itarabhujaṃ nāgabhoge nidhāya |
paścād bāhudvayena pratibhaṭaśamane dhārayan śaṅkhacakre
devībhūṣādijuṣṭo janayatu jagatāṃ śarma vaikuṇṭhanāthaḥ ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined, meditating on the Lord.
items.meaning: May the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, who removes the sins of those who take refuge in him, bring happiness to the worlds — his left foot stretched forward and the right drawn up, his right hand resting on the knee and the other arm laid on the coils of the serpent, holding in his two rear hands the conch and the discus that quell his foes, attended by the Goddess and adorned with his ornaments.

items.text: Now recite the aṣṭākṣara mantra, as taught by your ācārya, {japaCount} times (or as many times as you resolved). It is not printed here.

todo: This step is only for those who have received initiation (samāśrayaṇam) from an ācārya (teacher).
Recite the taniyans (verses of praise) of your ācārya-paramparā (line of teachers).
Do prāṇāyāma three times, using the aṣṭākṣara mantra in place of the prāṇāyāma mantra.
Then do the nyāsa and the dhyāna verse.
Recite the aṣṭākṣara mantra as many times as you resolved for the Gāyatrī.
Do this step at the point your ācārya or family teaches; families differ on where it goes.

text.iast:
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam |
oṃ tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||
oṃ āpo̱ jyotī̱ raso̱'mṛta̱ṃ brahma̱ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̱rom ||

items.action: Recite silently while holding your breath, as in the Prāṇāyāmam step.
items.meaning: Om, the seven worlds. We meditate on the adorable light of the divine Creator; may He guide our intellect. He is the waters, the light, the flavour and the nectar of immortality, and fills the three worlds.

text.iast: mamopātta samasta duritakṣaya dvārā śrī parameśvara prītyarthaṃ {kala} sandhyopasthānaṃ kariṣye ||

items.action: Say the saṅkalpa in the saṅkalpa posture.
items.meaning: For the destruction of all my sins and to please the Supreme Lord, I shall perform the upasthānam of the {kalaEn} sandhyā.

text.iast: śrī bhagavadājñayā śrīmannārāyaṇa prītyarthaṃ {kala} sandhyā upasthānaṃ kariṣye ||

items.action: Say the saṅkalpa in the saṅkalpa posture.
items.meaning: By the command of the Lord and for the pleasure of Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, I shall perform the upasthānam of the {kalaEn} sandhyā.

items.action: Stand up and touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the anuvāka beginning *uttame* the seer is Vāmadeva.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metre is anuṣṭup.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is Gāyatrī.

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: It is used for taking leave of Gāyatrī.

text.iast:
u̱ttame̍ śikha̍re de̱vī̱ bhū̱myāṃ pa̍rvata̱mūrdha̍ni |
brā̱hmaṇe̎bhyo hya̍nujñā̱na̱ṃ ga̱ccha de̍vi ya̱thā su̍kham ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined, then open them outward (udvāsana mudrā).
items.meaning: O Goddess, having granted your leave to the brāhmaṇas, return at your pleasure to your abode on the highest peak, on the summit of the mountain on earth.

items.text: Some families do the aṣṭākṣara japam at this point instead of right after the Gāyatrī japam.

todo: Do prāṇāyāma three times, as in the Prāṇāyāmam step.
Take the saṅkalpa posture and resolve to do the upasthānam (the Sun salutation in the next step).
Stand up and do the nyāsa.
With palms joined in añjali, recite *Uttame śikhare* to take leave of the Goddess.
Open your joined palms outward (the *udvāsana mudrā*).

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the upasthāna mantras beginning *mitrasya* the seer is Viśvāmitra.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metres are gāyatrī and triṣṭup.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is Mitra.

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: They are used in the Sun salutation of the morning sandhyā.

text.iast:
mi̱trasya̍ carṣaṇī̱ dhṛta̱śśravo̍ de̱vasya̍ sāna̱sim |
sa̱tyaṃ ci̱tra śra̍vastamam ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: I praise the glory of the divine Mitra, upholder of peoples — glory that is easily won, true and most wondrous to hear.

text.iast:
mi̱tro janā̍n yātayati prajā̱nan mi̱tro dā̍dhāra pṛthi̱vīm u̱ta dyām |
mi̱traḥ kṛ̱ṣṭīr ani̍miṣā̱'bhica̍ṣṭe sa̱tyāya̍ ha̱vyaṃ ghṛ̱tava̍d vidhema ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: Mitra, all-knowing, sets people to their tasks; Mitra upholds the earth and the heaven. Mitra gazes with unclosing eyes upon all mankind; to the True One let us offer the oblation soaked in ghee.

text.iast:
pra sa mi̍tra̱ marto̍ astu̱ praya̍svā̱n yasta̍ āditya̱ śikṣa̍ti vra̱tena̍ |
na ha̍nyate̱ na jī̍yate̱ tvoto̱ naina̱m aguṃho̍ aśno̱ty anti̍to̱ na dū̱rāt ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: O Mitra, O Āditya, may the mortal who serves you with his vow and offerings prosper: protected by you he is neither slain nor overcome, and sin does not reach him from near or from far.

text.iast: āsatyenety ādi mantrāṇāṃ hiraṇyastūpa viśvāmitra kutsa vasiṣṭhā ṛṣayaḥ |

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the mantras beginning *ā satyena* the seers are Hiraṇyastūpa, Viśvāmitra, Kutsa and Vasiṣṭha.

text.iast: triṣṭup gāyatrī jagatī uṣṇik triṣṭup chandāguṃsi |

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metres are triṣṭup, gāyatrī, jagatī, uṣṇik and triṣṭup.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is Āditya.

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: They are used in the Sun salutation of the midday sandhyā.

text.iast:
ā sa̱tyena̱ raja̍sā̱ varta̍māno nive̱śaya̍nn a̱mṛta̱ṃ martya̍ñ ca |
hi̱ra̱ṇyaye̍na savi̱tā rathe̱nā''de̱vo yā̍ti̱ bhuva̍nā vi̱paśya̍n ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: Moving through the shining realm with truth, settling the immortal and the mortal in their places, the god Savitā comes in his golden chariot, beholding all the worlds.

text.iast:
ud va̱yaṃ tama̍sa̱s pari̱ paśya̍nto̱ jyoti̱r utta̍ram |
de̱vaṃ de̍va̱trā sūrya̱m aga̍nma̱ jyoti̍r utta̱mam ||
udu̱tyaṃ jā̱tave̍dasaṃ de̱vaṃ va̍hanti ke̱tava̍ḥ | dṛ̱śe viśvā̍ya̱ sūrya̍m ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: Looking up beyond the darkness to the higher light, we have reached Sūrya, god among gods, the highest light. Up rises that god Sūrya, knower of all beings, borne by his rays — for all to see.

text.iast:
ci̱traṃ de̱vānā̱m uda̍gā̱d anī̍kaṃ cakṣu̍r mi̱trasya̱ varu̍ṇasyā̱gneḥ |
ā prā̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī a̱ntari̍kṣa̱guṃ sūrya̍ ā̱tmā jaga̍tas ta̱sthuṣa̍ś ca ||
tac cakṣu̍r de̱vahi̍taṃ pu̱rastā̎c chu̱kram u̱ccara̍t |

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: The wondrous face of the gods has risen — the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni; Sūrya, the Self of all that moves and stands, has filled heaven, earth and the atmosphere. That bright eye set by the gods rises in the east.

text.iast: paśye̍ma śa̱rada̍śśa̱taṃ | jīve̍ma śa̱rada̍śśa̱taṃ | nandā̍ma śa̱rada̍śśa̱taṃ | modā̍ma śa̱rada̍śśa̱taṃ | bhavā̍ma śa̱rada̍śśa̱taṃ | śṛṇavā̍ma śa̱rada̍śśa̱taṃ | prabra̍vāma śa̱rada̍śśa̱taṃ | ajī̍tāsyāma śa̱rada̍śśa̱taṃ | jyok ca̱ sūrya̍ṃ dṛ̱śe ||

items.action: Look at the sun through the vyoma mudrā while you say this.
items.meaning: May we see for a hundred autumns, may we live for a hundred autumns, may we rejoice for a hundred autumns, may we be glad for a hundred autumns, may we flourish for a hundred autumns, may we hear for a hundred autumns, may we speak well for a hundred autumns, may we be undefeated for a hundred autumns — and long may we behold the Sun.

text.iast: ya uda̍gān maha̱to'rṇavā̎t vi̱bhrāja̍mānaḥ sari̱rasya̱ madhyā̱t sa mā̍ vṛṣa̱bho lo̍hitā̱kṣassūryo̍ vipa̱ścin mana̍sā punātu ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: He who has risen out of the great ocean, blazing from the midst of the waters — may that Sun, the strong bull, red-eyed and all-seeing, purify me in mind.

text.iast: imaṃ me varuṇety ādi mantrāṇāṃ devarāta ṛṣiḥ |

items.action: Touch the top of your head.
items.meaning: Of the mantras beginning *imaṃ me varuṇa* the seer is Devarāta.

items.action: Touch the tip of your nose.
items.meaning: The metres are gāyatrī, triṣṭup and jagatī.

items.action: Touch your heart.
items.meaning: The deity is Varuṇa.

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: They are used in the Sun salutation of the evening sandhyā.

text.iast: i̱maṃ me̍ varuṇa śrudhī̱ hava̍m a̱dyā ca̍ mṛḍaya | tvām a̍va̱syur āca̍ke ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: O Varuṇa, hear this my call and be gracious even now; seeking your protection I approach you.

text.iast:
tat tvā̍ yāmi̱ brahma̍ṇā̱ vanda̍mānas ta̱dā śā̎ste̱ yaja̍māno ha̱virbhi̍ḥ |
ahe̍ḍamāno varuṇe̱ha bo̱dhy uru̍śaguṃsa̱ mā na̱ āyu̱ḥ pra mo̍ṣīḥ ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: Praising you with prayer I approach you for that which the sacrificer seeks with his oblations. O Varuṇa of wide renown, be not angry; take heed of us here, and do not steal away our life.

text.iast:
yac ci̱d dhi te̱ viśo̍ yathā̱ pra de̍va varuṇa vra̱tam |
mi̱nī̱masi̱ dyavi̍dyavi ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: Whatever your laws, O god Varuṇa, we break day after day, as ordinary people do.

text.iast:
yat kiñce̱daṃ va̍ruṇa̱ daivye̱ jane̍'bhidro̱haṃ ma̍nu̱ṣyā̎ś carā̍masi |
aci̍ttī̱ yat tava̱ dharmā̍ yuyopi̱ma mā na̱s tasmā̱d ena̍so deva rīriṣaḥ ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: Whatever wrong we humans have here committed against the divine folk, O Varuṇa; whatever of your laws we have broken through heedlessness — O god, do not harm us for that sin.

text.iast:
ki̱ta̱vāso̱ yad ri̍ri̱pur na dī̱vi yad vā̍ ghā sa̱tyam u̱ta yan na vi̱dma |
sarvā̱ tā vi ṣya̍ śithi̱reva̍ de̱vāthā̍ te syāma varuṇa pri̱yāsa̍ḥ ||

items.action: Say this with your palms joined.
items.meaning: Whatever wrong was done, like gamblers cheating at play; whatever we did knowingly, and whatever we know not — loosen all these from us, O god, like slackened bonds, and may we be dear to you, O Varuṇa.

todo: Stand with your palms joined in añjali.
Do the nyāsa for your time of day.

todo.text: For the vyoma (gālinī) mudrā, place your left palm up and your right palm down.
Fold the middle and ring fingers of both hands inward.
Put your right index finger over your left little finger, and your right little finger over your left index finger.
Tuck the folded fingers under the opposite thumbs, leaving a small slit between your hands.
